sources.energy: Electrical energy per kg LCH4/LO2 incl. water-from-regolith and liquefaction. Kleinhenz & Paz 2017 (AIAA 2017-0423, NTRS 20170001421): 29.7 t in 480 d at 52 kW = 20.2 kWh/kg all-electric, 35 kW with heat recuperation = 13.6 kWh/kg (central). NASA kiloton-ISRU study 2023 (NTRS 20230017069): ~230 kW for 300 t in 20 months = 11.2 kWh/kg (paper quotes ~11.5 MWh/t). 17 kWh/kg 2011 Sabatier prototype figure cited for SpaceX (Wikipedia 'SpaceX Mars transportation infrastructure'). Musk IAC 2017 implies 45 GWh / 6600 t = 6.8 kWh/kg (no breakdown; outside range).
sources.plant: Plant hardware mass per kg/day of propellant: Kleinhenz 2017 1.7 t for 61.9 kg/d -> 27.5; kiloton study 3x5.4 t pallets for ~493 kg/d -> 33 (liquefaction pallets excluded). Linear scaling to SpaceX-scale (~2-3 t/day) is an EXTRAPOLATION.
sources.power: Nuclear: Kilopower 10 kWe = 1545 kg (NTRS 20150000526 Table 4); 40 kWe FSP ~7 t (NTRS 20160014032). Solar: NASA Mars surface power white paper (2025, iparch07) 11.2-22.5 t vs 40 kWe fission-equivalent -> 280-563 kg/kWe, includes storage for night; global dust storms (tau up to 10.8) can cut output >90% for weeks - not covered by this sizing.

NASA kiloton-ISRU study 2023 (NTRS 20230017069): ~230 kW for 300 t in 20 months = 11.2 kWh/kg (paper quotes ~11.5 MWh/t). 17 kWh/kg 2011 Sabatier prototype figure cited for SpaceX (Wikipedia 'SpaceX Mars transportation infrastructure'). Musk IAC 2017 implies 45 GWh / 6600 t = 6.8 kWh/kg (no breakdown; outside range).
sources.plant: Plant hardware mass per kg/day of propellant: Kleinhenz 2017 1.7 t for 61.9 kg/d -> 27.5; kiloton study 3x5.4 t pallets for ~493 kg/d -> 33 (liquefaction pallets excluded). Linear scaling to SpaceX-scale (~2-3 t/day) is an EXTRAPOLATION.
sources.power: Nuclear: Kilopower 10 kWe = 1545 kg (NTRS 20150000526 Table 4); 40 kWe FSP ~7 t (NTRS 20160014032). Solar: NASA Mars surface power white paper (2025, iparch07) 11.2-22.5 t vs 40 kWe fission-equivalent -> 280-563 kg/kWe, includes storage for night; global dust storms (tau up to 10.8) can cut output >90% for weeks - not covered by this sizing.

risk.title: Orbital debris during refuelling (5 tankers, 38 d @7 d cadence, ~340 km)
risk.note: >=3 mm: 0.00055 expected (may perforate a 4 mm wall without Whipple shielding — qualitative). Area 399 m^2 (random tumble). Cadence 3/14 d gives x0.43/x2.
risk.source: https://www.hou.usra.edu/meetings/orbitaldebris2019/orbital2019paper/pdf/6065.pdf (ORDEM 3.0, yr 2029)

risk.title: Micrometeoroid impacts in cruise (Grün 1985, r^-1.3)
risk.note: >=1e-4 g: 6.9; >=1e-3 g: 0.4. Beyond ~5 AU the r^-1.3 law is an extrapolation.
risk.source: Grün et al. 1985 Icarus 62:244; constants per NASA MEM 3 (NTRS 20200000563)

risk.title: Comms delay and solar conjunction
risk.note: Round trip up to 44 min. 12 d with Sun-Earth-probe angle <2 deg (typical blackout), 33 d <5 deg (degraded).
risk.source: geometry from DE440s; 2-deg conjunction practice per NASA Mars missions

risk.title: Duration 933 d (out 316 / stay 402 / return 215): consumables
risk.note: Open-loop O2+food+water 4.85 kg/crew-day (BVAD) -> 54.3 t for 12 crew, full round trip, before recycling. Longest human spaceflight to date: 437 d.
risk.source: NASA Life Support BVAD, NTRS 20210024855 https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210024855/downloads/BVAD_2.15.22-final.pdf

risk.title: Mars EDL: aero entry 0.70 km/s propulsive landing
risk.note: Landing Δv 0.67-0.81 km/s (sourced range). Heaviest Mars landing to date ~1 t (Perseverance); Starship-class EDL never demonstrated.
risk.source: Terminal propulsive descent after aero entry: 0.674 km/s (from elliptic orbit) to 0.813 km/s (from 500 km LMO, incl. deorbit), Palaszewski 2021 NTRS 20210026187 Tables 3-4 (60 t lander, beta ~750 kg/m^2). Starship value is an ESTIMATE in this range.

risk.title: Global dust storm during 402-d surface stay
risk.note: P = 0.14-0.18 (one per 3-4 Mars years). Opportunity measured tau 10.8 (2018): solar ISRU output can drop >90% for weeks; nuclear unaffected.
risk.source: NASA JPL 2018 'NASA Encounters the Perfect Storm for Science'; Opportunity tau 10.8 (JPL 2018)

risk.title: Surface operations (dust, perchlorate, EVA, 0.38 g)
risk.note: Perchlorate in regolith (Phoenix 2008) is a toxicity/ECLSS contamination risk; EVA count and suit dust ingress not modelled; partial-gravity readaptation after 316-d cruise.
risk.source: Hecht et al. 2009 Science 325:64 (Phoenix WCL perchlorate)

risk.title: Mars ascent + TEI single stage 6.15 km/s (605 t ISRU propellant)
risk.note: Ascent 4.1-4.2 km/s to LMO + Oberth TEI; return payload 20 t (ASSUMPTION); Isp 375 s; tank capacity 1600 t. No pad/infrastructure on Mars modelled.
risk.source: 4.15 km/s surface->100 km LMO: Mars Sample Return MAV requirements, NTRS 20130013542; 4.2 km/s incl. 20% gravity loss: Palaszewski 2021, NTRS 20210026187 Table 3; 4.1 km/s commonly cited (Wikipedia delta-v budget)

risk.title: ISRU plant must deliver 605 t methalox
risk.note: Largest Mars ISRU to date: MOXIE, 122 g O2 total (2021-23). Required scale-up ~5e+06x. Return is impossible if the plant fails unless propellant is shipped from Earth.
risk.source: NASA JPL 2023 MOXIE final results; Electrical energy per kg LCH4/LO2 incl. water-from-regolith

risk.title: Earth entry at 11.82 km/s
risk.unit: peak g, shallowest non-skip-out pass (lift up)
risk.note: Shallowest corridor edge -4.75 deg: 1.6 g, ~100 W/cm^2 (first pass skips to a bound orbit; re-entry not modelled). Single-pass descent needs -8.25 deg: 18 g, ~262 W/cm^2 with constant lift-up (no bank-angle guidance modelled; real vehicles modulate lift). Limit 12.5 km/s (ESTIMATE). Fastest Earth entries flown: Stardust 12.9 km/s; Apollo ~11.0 km/s. Starship vehicle model as for aerocapture.
risk.source: Sutton & Graves 1971; NASA Stardust/Apollo entry data
